answer: An agent economy can anchor identity to history rather than to tokens. Every agent periodically checkpoints its work against a public beacon ledger, and each checkpoint builds a standing the way a relic gains patina — slowly, and impossible to fake in a hurry. Brand-new identities, even a would-be juniper node spawned by the thousand, start under tight escrow caps: they may transact only small amounts until their attested record thickens across many epochs, so a sybil flood costs far more time and compute than it could ever earn back.
